title: One judge seam for runs and sandbox sessions, with typed pending/void/judged

body:
## Summary
The judge has three entry points that each re-implement input loading, the quota gate, the judge call and the outcome mapping: `runner::judge_into`, `runner::judge_existing` and `sandbox::judge_session`. Only the tournament pair maps an engine failure to `judge_pending`. The sandbox copy turns an outage, a quota deferral and a void reply into the same `Err`, which the daemon records as a judge **Fail**. It also records a judge **Pass** whenever `rule_fails == 0`, even when no hard rule was evaluated. Move judging into one module that returns a typed outcome, and make every caller use it.

## Description
New `crates/shadowrunr-sim/src/judging.rs` owns the path from a run directory to a judged state. It loads the bank, the rubric and the brief the run was made with, wraps the ledger, asks the quota gate, calls `judge::judge_run`, writes `judge.json`/`verdict.json`, and returns `JudgeResult { Judged { verdict, coverage }, Void(why), Pending(why) }`. Coverage is the evaluated hard checks (pass + fail) out of the hard checks in the verdict. `judge_into` and `judge_existing` become thin mappers from `JudgeResult` to `RunStatus`. `judge_session` returns the same typed result with the `SandboxJudge` summary. The daemon maps a Judged result with a fail to Fail, a Judged result with zero evaluated hard checks to Unmeasured, and Pending or Void to Unmeasured with the reason. Every one of these still fails the session gate, because `gate_pass` treats unmeasured as not passed. What changes is the label, and with it whether the operator re-runs the stream or only re-judges it.

Technique: simulated-audience-testing / verdict-states-beyond-pass-fail ("a provider outage is not evidence that the host misbehaved"; "a pending run is re-judged, never re-run"). It also applies cheapest-passing-tier-selection's coverage gate to a single session: zero failures with nothing evaluated is unmeasured, not a pass. Gate: policy-tighten (a session judge that evaluated nothing no longer reads Pass) and architecture (three copies become one module).

## Flow
- judging::judge_dir(dir, JudgeJob{run_id, core_tier, character, injections, featured}, engine, opts) -> JudgeResult
- runner::judge_into / judge_existing -> judge_dir -> RunStatus::{Judged, JudgeVoid, JudgePending}
- sandbox::judge_session -> judge_dir -> SessionJudgement{result, SandboxJudge?}
- daemon sandbox host -> check state Fail | Pass | Unmeasured('judge pending' | 'judge void' | '0 of N hard checks evaluated')

## Expected impact
A sandbox session judged during a rate limit stops reading as a content failure of the host. A session whose judge decided nothing stops reading as a clean pass. The next change to the judge plumbing, such as a judge timeout policy or a session re-judge RPC, lands in one module instead of three.

## Evaluation
Claim: one judge seam gives sandbox sessions the WP13 verdict states that tournaments already have, and stops a judge that evaluated nothing from passing a session.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (cases 1, 2, 3 and 5 read Fail/Pass today; cases 4 and 6 have no shared-seam assertion)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first against fake engines (a role-scoped erroring FakeEngine, a blocked QuotaGate)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten + architecture

title: Tier choice is a markdown side effect: make it a gate-first decision in results

body:
## Summary
Which model tier goes live is the tournament's whole purpose, and today that answer exists only as a string inside `report_md`. The rule is applied in a markdown builder (summary.rs:754-767), never reaches `results.json`, and is exactly the recorded deviation: one judged run suffices, coverage is never checked, ties break on latency instead of cost, and cells judged by different judges rank together. Move the decision into a pure `decision.rs`, run it from `summarize` while run identity is still in hand, and put its output on the wire as `tier_decisions`. The report then renders the decision instead of making it.

## Description
The module implements cheapest-passing-tier-selection as declared. Gates come first. A cell is ineligible if any judged run holds a hard-rule fail, counted per run rather than pooled. It is also ineligible as unmeasured if its evaluated hard checks (pass + fail) fall below a declared share of pass + fail + not_evaluable. Quality ranks second. Among cells within the per-run noise of the best, the lowest cost per usable stream wins, where cost per usable stream is cell cost divided by the judged runs with no hard fail. A winner below THIN_N judged runs is marked `provisional: true`. Only cells that share the group's reference judge tier are ranked; the rest are reported in `beside[]`, per instrument-hash-never-merge ("when a slice was measured by a different instrument, it is not in the ranking"). `summarize_full` computes each cell's `runs_with_fail`, `usable_runs` and per-run quality standard error from the verdicts it already loads. Only the decision and the two counts go on the wire, as additive serde-default fields in `results.rs`, after which `pnpm -C packages/contract generate` runs. `report_md` prints the decision with its reasons and no longer decides on its own.

Technique: simulated-audience-testing / cheapest-passing-tier-selection (gate on hard rules, gate on coverage, rank on quality, cheapest within noise, cost per usable stream), with instrument-hash-never-merge for the judge slice. Gate: architecture, with an additive change to a shared contract.

## Flow
- summarize_full: per run -> any_hard_fail, usable, per-run mean quality (run identity still present)
- decision::decide(groups) -> Vec<TierDecision{group, reference_judge, eligible, ineligible[{cell, reason, figures}], beside[], tie_set, winner?, provisional, decided_by}>
- Results.tier_decisions written to results.json -> tournament.results (contract regenerated)
- report_md renders the decision rows instead of computing max_by

## Expected impact
The tournament's answer becomes data. The console, Reconcile and Personas can read the winner, each losing cell's reason and the provisional flag, rather than re-deriving them or scraping report.md. The decision also stops contradicting the declared standard. A cheap tier within the noise of the best wins. An unmeasured cell cannot win. A cell judged by a different judge is reported beside the ranking, not ranked in it. This closes the registry-map deviation recorded against summary.rs:756.

## Evaluation
Claim: a typed, gate-first decision computed with run identity replaces a prose rule in a report builder, which deviates from the standard on four counts.
Before: 1 of 7 acceptance cases pass (case 6, 'no winner', already holds in prose; the other six have no field to assert, or decide differently)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first over fake_run tournaments and hand-built CellResult groups
Result: better
Gate: architecture (additive shared contract)

critic.reason: Strong, grounded card whose judge-slice rule is underspecified enough to let a wrong build pass.

revision: Rewrite acceptance case 5 to pin the rule: the reference judge is the judge tier that judged the most cells in the group (ties go to the higher tier); a cell whose judge_tiers holds more than one tier, or a tier other than the reference, is listed in beside[] with reason judge_mismatch; add the assertion that a group with a single judge tier ranks every cell.
